data.exact_reserve_text: Over-provision in respect of prior claims and claim adjustment expenses

prior_year_events.impact_description: Benign loss activity in 2016 calendar years contributed to a strong profit for the 2016 pure year, particularly from reinsurance and insurance property accounts.

Majority of 2017 hurricane losses arising from reinsurance business impacted the 2017 year of account, and direct property losses impacted both the 2016 and 2017 years of account, leading to adverse development.

named_events.loss_description: Losses from Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria were almost entirely in 2017 year of account, impacting reinsurance and direct property losses for 2016 and 2017 years of account.

The 2018 account will pick up almost all of the reinsurance loss from the 2018 hurricane, typhoon and wildfire losses together with a relatively modest share of direct property loss.

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate experienced a gross release of $390.991 million in prior year reserves, primarily due to an overall over-provision for claims and claim adjustment expenses. This favorable development was influenced by benign loss activity in 2016, particularly in reinsurance and insurance property accounts, and releases from closed years of 2015 and prior, partly related to Reinsurance to Close (RITC) adjustments spread across various classes. However, this was partially offset by adverse development from 2017 hurricanes (Harvey, Irma, and Maria) which impacted both reinsurance business and direct property losses for the 2016 and 2017 years of account.

data.data_quality_notes: The narrative mentions a net release of $70.6 million from 2015 and prior years due to RITC, which is a component of the overall prior year development. While the gross prior year development figure is explicitly stated, the RITC could introduce distortions if attempting to derive prior year development solely from the claims development triangle.
